flags: minor: passage says the eruption 'killed thousands'; historical estimates are roughly 10,000 direct deaths and tens of thousands in all. 'Thousands' is technically true but understates it.
minor: 'an ocean away' (para 3) undersells the Indonesia-to-New England/Europe distance; 'half a planet away' in para 1 is the more accurate phrasing.
R024-01.notes: The passage is built around distant effects (New England, Europe, Geneva) and the point that the average figure hides what matters. A is never discussed. C reverses the final paragraph. D: Sumbawa gets one sentence and nothing is compared. B is the only option that covers the whole passage, though it underplays the cultural paragraph a little.

R024-02.notes: Para 2 states it directly: the sulfur haze 'reflected part of the incoming sunlight back into space.' C is a trap taken from the mistaken 1816 belief in para 3. A and B are not in the passage.

R024-03.notes: 'Modest when averaged ... less than one degree Celsius' means small in size. 'Humble' is the familiar trap meaning but does not fit a temperature figure.

R024-04.notes: Para 2 ends with 'averages can hide a great deal,' and para 3 then gives concrete harms: snow, frosts, rotted harvests, riots. B is wrong because Europe is also named. A and D describe other paragraphs.

R024-05.notes: 'Few people ... had even heard of the eruption, and no one yet understood how a volcano could change the weather.' A is the opposite trap. D contradicts 'never thought about the upper atmosphere.' C is not supported. This is close to a stated detail despite the word 'inferred.'

flags: minor: para 4 states this almost outright ('matters less than when the cold arrives'), so 'suggests' overstates how much inference is needed. It sits near the easy/medium line.
R024-06.notes: Timing during the growing season is the author's explicit point. B misreads 'several degrees' (para 4) and contradicts 'less than one degree' (para 2). C misuses the hypothetical cold winter from para 4. D is too extreme.

flags: Overlap with R024-08: both test the same sentence, the author's qualification of 'the volcano produced the novel.' 07's choice D ('qualify a popular claim') signals 08's answer B ('skeptical'), and 08's B in turn confirms 07's D. Consider replacing one of the two items.
R024-07.notes: The final paragraph adds a 'cultural trace' (Frankenstein) and then qualifies the popular telling ('more accurate to say the weather supplied the occasion'). B is an extreme overstatement. A and C describe other paragraphs.

flags: Overlap with R024-07 (see flag there): the same sentence is tested twice and each item's choices give away the other's answer.
R024-08.notes: The author says it is 'more accurate to say that the weather supplied the occasion; the ideas were already Shelley's own,' which matches B almost word for word. C: the author never doubts the contest. D: the author takes a clear position. A ignores the qualification.
